newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 12.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton repeated his belief that a new IRA ceasefire was inevitable, expressing his hope that a ceasefire "will occur soon".
- Two of Ireland's largest trade unions are meeting on Thursday to discuss the merits of entering another national wage agreement with the government and employers.
- Independent Newspapers notched up pre-tax profits of one million punts per week in the first six months of 1996.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on his visit to Washington that multi-party peace talks in Belfast must get down to real business quickly, or miss a window of opportunity.

- The government will be unable to spend money in support of a November referendum on changing the bail laws, because of a legal ruling that their use of taxpayers' money to promote last year's divorce referendum was unconstitutional.
- The government is to place a price cap on state telecom company Telecom Eireann to keep its average prices well below the rate of inflation for a two to five year period.
- The government was accused by the Irish Small and Medium Enterprises Association (ISME) of contributing to low wages and high unemployment through excessive public spending and high taxation.
